subject.title: fix(codex): require explicit final source delivery

question: Should Codex message-tool-only completion use an explicit model-facing `final` contract with omission reserved for legacy terminal behavior, or should OpenClaw retain implicit completion and use final-only prompt guidance?
rationale: The competing approaches create different durable runtime and plugin API contracts; maintainers must select the permanent boundary after the prompt/runtime defect is repaired.

options.title: Adopt explicit boolean intent
options.body: Require `final:false` for progress and `final:true` for completion, preserve omission only for legacy terminal callers, and prove all three cases.

options.title: Use prompt-only guidance
options.body: Retain implicit confirmed-delivery completion and use the narrower proof-positive prompt-only candidate.

options.title: Redesign omission semantics
options.body: Make omission non-terminal too, accepting a broader compatibility change with explicit upgrade proof.

recommendation.title: Adopt explicit boolean intent
recommendation.body: Require `final:false` for progress and `final:true` for completion, preserve omission only for legacy terminal callers, and prove all three cases.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged feature defines the existing terminal-delivery compatibility behavior this decision would change.
